title: System Boundaries
hook: Sometimes you can't fix a problem because you drew the box around it way too small.
statement: What you include in the problem decides what you can actually control.
explainer: If churn is the problem but you only look at support, you'll miss the onboarding or the sales promises causing it. Zoom out and the fix often gets obvious.
sop: Write down the current scope of the problem you're solving.
Score Scope Considered, how much of the bigger picture you included, 1 to 10.
Name one upstream and one downstream factor you've left out.
Redraw the boundary to include at least one of them.
Solve it again at the new scope before calling it fixed.
equation_example: Outcomes Achieved 4, Scope Considered 3. (4 + 3) ÷ 2 = 3.5. Low on both usually means the problem was framed too narrowly, not solved badly. Higher means you're working on the real system.
question: Take one stuck problem and write one upstream and one downstream factor you've been ignoring.
closing_statement: How you draw the boundary decides what you can fix.
caption:
Principle Nº 124: System Boundaries

Sometimes you can't fix a problem because you drew the box around it way too small.

What you include in the problem decides what you can actually control.

Your turn: Take one stuck problem and write one upstream and one downstream factor you've been ignoring.
